ALDICARB DOG POISONING

By: Ntokozo Miya | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We hold the SAPS accountable for failure to enforce laws regulate the use and possession of the highly toxic and prohibited substance Aldicarb.

Unique Selling Point:
Dr Verdoorn will illustrate the high toxicity of Aldicarb as well as the poison's effects not only on rats and dogs, but also on humans.

Summary:
The Griffon Poison Information Centre (GPIC) says that dog deaths by poisoning are on the rise, and it is mainly due to a banned pesticide commonly used as rat poison. As many as 1 000 dogs die in SA each week due to poison.
Aldicarb is a highly toxic pesticide that is illegal to use and possess in South Africa. However, people from neighbouring countries where the substance is still in use bring it into the country in bulk and sell it on the black market as rat poison.
Aldicarb is notoriously known as 'two-step' (because you take 2 steps and you die) and 'aliphirimi' (the sun will not rise – because you will not see the next sunrise if you ingest it). It is deadly to rats, dogs and humans.
Criminals often use Aldicarb to kill dogs at a property they wish to rob. The poison is placed inside sausages, wors or viennas, thrown over the fence for the dog to eat and criminals return some time later to rob the home, without the dogs alerting the sleeping owners. That is prevalent in the suburbs whereas in townships, many dogs die after accidentally ingesting Aldicarb which has been laid out in the open for rats.
Aldicarb is easily available at most taxi ranks and some spaza shops and is preferred by many as rat poison because it is cheap. It sells for around R10 for a dosage which is enough to deal with rat infestation for the whole house, or kill an adult human.

Further information:
We explore the high toxicity of Aldicarb and question why authorities are failing to eradicate the sale and use of the substance. This is an important discussion considering that the substance is also noted to be responsible for around 100 murders in Johannesburg each year and is also preferred as an effective poison to commit suicide.

Our speakers expand on the dangers of Aldicarb not only to animals but also humans - Dr Verdoorn tells confirms the number above of 100 murders committed using Aldicarb in Johannesburg each year. Dr Verdoorn and Cora Bailey also give examples of when Aldicarb was used to commit suicide. The insert includes links that further highlight the seriousness of the consequences of using and being in possession of Aldicarb - it is literally a murder weapon for just R10 a pop, cheaper than murder weapons such as a gun and even a knife. We highlight this in our questioning to the police - if they would not ignore someone selling guns willy nilly on the streets, why are they then being so careless when it comes to Aldicarb salespeople, despite that the problem has around for many years. Another link will be done with the presenter interacting with dogs. All our speakers mention and one extensively discusses the criminality behind Aldicarb, dog poisonings and it being used as a murder weapon e.g. it being mixed in with the intended victim's popular food, the speed with which Aldicarb works (which makes it preferred for suicide). In our voice-overs we give examples of incidents of human deaths linked to Aldicarb. The SPCA also explains that when confronted with a high number of call-outs where dog poisoning is concerned, they alert the police as such incidents usually point to planned housebreakings. When filming the doctor's interview, he will show us just how little is needed to make the drug fatal to not just animals but more importantly to humans too. The insert also illustrates how easily available the drug is and that dealers are only too happy to sell the stuff in bulk. The SPCA and Cora share images of call-outs relevant to the topic and express their frustration at the prevalence of Aldicarb on the streets as well as police disregard for the Aldicarb use and possession. "Thabo" is a reformed housebreaker who cements the link between Aldicarb and crime by sharing how he used Aldicarb on many occasions when he went breaking into people's homes.

Script:


FINAL ALDICARB SCRIPT


AUDIO

CHANTAL LABUSCHAGNE – DOG OWNER

We've had this puppy for 8 years so it's been a big part [cries] of our family…..

VO -- Two weeks ago Chantal Labuschagne’s Yorkie - Max became violently ill…

CHANTAL LABUSCHAGNE – DOG OWNER

When I called the dog, he was crawling. He couldn't even walk….. It was less than 5 minutes and our dog was dead.

VO -- Hours later, the family’s second dog – a great Dane called Sheba – began vomiting… …

CHANTAL LABUSCHAGNE – DOG OWNER

So, we've got the great dane running around still looking fine and the next morning, we wake up with our red-eyed. He also passed away in his own vomit….

LINK - Imagine finding the family dog lying in your driveway, cold and unresponsive. Well, this was the reality for Roodepoort residents last month where close to forty dogs were poisoned.

VO – On the 31st of July - dogs in a small block in Roodepoort, west of Johannesburg were targeted in a co-ordinated poison attack…

Annica Pretorious of the SPCA explains the initial signs of a poisoning...

ANNICA PRETORIOUS – ROODEPOORT SPCA

They start vomiting. They start convulsing. They go into seizures. The 40 is actually not the dogs that were poisoned – those are the dogs that passed away.

VO – APCAN Security's Gerhard Oberholzer says this is an old criminal tactic where dogs in a home are silenced with poison so criminals can break into a property without raising the alarm.

GERHARD OBERHOLZER – APCAN SECURITY

Within a day, a 24-hour period, there's a second criminal transgression where they have either broken into a vehicle, stolen a trailer.

MAC – What pushes criminals to target a specific area?

If you have a well-kept garden or you drive a nice vehicle – they know what resources go into it. We get calls 2 to 3 times a week and that's just to us. That's not someone who goes directly to the police for instance.







VO – On that night, even more pets in the area were poisoned but many were saved after receiving immediate medical attention.

But others weren’t so lucky.. in this CCTV footage… two dogs are seen barking at suspects seemingly staking out the property… these animals were later found dead by their owners.

Following this mass poisoning, security companies increased patrols and visibility to discourage thieves.

But two days after the Labuschagne’s dogs were killed… their home was broken into.

CHANTAL LABUSCHAGNE – DOG OWNER

They climbed over the wall and just came in and helped themselves to the children's bicycles and my husband's motorbike.

VO – Dr Gerhard Verdoorn has over twenty years’ experience, researching the links between dog poisonings and criminality for the Griffon Poison Information Centre, and says criminals prefer using a well-known agricultural pesticide called Aldicarb.

GERHARD VERDOORN – GRIFFON POISON INFROMATION CENTRE

It is more toxic to dogs than to other mammals.

VO – Aldicarb is banned in South Africa. It is illegal to possess, sell and use in any form. But this deadly chemical is still a popular poison to kill rats.

Smuggled in mainly from some neighbouring countries, it’s easily available on the streets of Johannesburg…

GERHARD VERDOORN – GRIFFON POISON INFROMATION CENTRE

If you get caught with Aldicarb, you get a R1 000 fine and/or 2 years penalty for every sachet you carry with you.

VO – Dr Verdoorn says nearly a thousand dogs are poisoned around the country each week.

Across the city in Vosloorus east of Joburg, Lebogang Sekgaile is still coming to terms with the poisoning of his dog.

LEBOGANG SEKGAILE – DOG OWNER

He was vomiting and there was a bit of blood there. After 30 minutes, my dog was gone.

VO – Then a few days later, his home was broken into.

LEBOGANG SEKGAILE – DOG OWNER

The home theatre system was not there. Some of my clothes were stolen. Electrical appliances were stolen.

VO – Police have neither made arrests in his case nor in the Labuschagne's.

Our informant…a reformed housebreaker…spent three years in prison for related crimes. He explains how the poison is used. (replaced second 'housebreaking with 'related crimes' to avoid having same word in sentence)

REFORMED HOUSEBREAKER

We cut open the vienna and then we put this thing called“haliphirimi”.

VO - The fast-acting nature of Aldicarb has earned it nicknames such as “haliphirimi”, a Sotho expression which says that you will not see another sunrise after taking the poison…

It’s also known as 2-step – because if enough is ingested, a victim could be dead after taking just 2 steps…

MAC – How much of it do you put inside the vienna?

REFORMED HOUSEBREAKER

We put in as much as we can. After we throw it in the yard, we leave and come back after an hour. Obviously the dogs will be dead, and then we go inside the house and take whatever we want to take.

LINK – Not all dog poisoning incidents are motivated by cruel intentions, some are purely accidental, with people trying to get rid of pests.

VO – And compared to other rat-killing chemicals, Aldicarb is the cheaper option.

UPSOUND

CB – How much is it? - SELLER 1 – R5

VO – The poison is mixed with food bits and left out for rats to consume. But pets can also easily eat the rat bait, says Cora Bailey of Community Led Animal Welfare.

CORA BAILEY – COMMUNITY LED ANIMAL WELFARE

I would say that more than 90 per cent of the cases we see are accidental poisonings. It obviously depends on how quickly they can get medical care. A huge number of them do die.

VO – In a disturbing coincidence, our interview was cut short when a stricken dog owner rushed in their dog - Danger - with symptoms of poisoning.

Danger was given a dose of charcoal to absorb the toxins in his stomach and then put on a drip.

The owner's quick actions saved Danger’s life.

Aldicarb is not only dangerous to animals, but it can prove deadly to humans too.

DR GERHARD VERDOORN – GRIFFON POISON INFORMATION CENTRE

It will be enough to kill 8 of us within about 20 minutes with this bit of Aldicarb. And if you inhale Aldicarb or you get Aldicarb on your skin, you're basically gone because it absorbs into the body.

MAC – How would you know that either this person or this dog has been killed as a result of ingesting Aldicarb?

DR GERHARD VERDOORN – GRIFFON POISON INFORMATION CENTRE

They find the black granules in the stomach contents of the animal or the human being.

VO - Traces of the substance left on harvested crops are just as harmful.

North America recorded one of its worst food-borne outbreaks of pesticide poisoning in 1985. More than two thousand people fell ill after eating contaminated watermelons.

In 2012, Chinese media reported that thirteen people died after eating laced cucumber.

Back home in 2017, a family of seven was treated for poisoning and two children passed away. But Dr Verdoorn cautions that death in humans isn’t always accidental.

DR GERHARD VERDOORN – GRIFFON POISON INFORMATION CENTRE

There are 100 people per year dying in the Gauteng area from ingestion of Aldicarb, that might be murders, it might be suicides. I'm currently working with the police on 3 murder cases.

LINK – Considering the toxicity and deadly effects of Aldicarb, why is it that law enforcers are seemingly oblivious to what is literally a murder weapon being sold openly on the streets?

VO – In this undercover footage, police officers casually walk past this Aldicarb trader outside a taxi rank in Johannesburg – without so much as giving him a warning. We requested an interview with the SAPS but we have yet to receive a response.

LINK – Despite still being distraught by the deaths of their pets, Roodepoort residents have some small cause for celebration.

VO – Last week, security guards apprehended a suspect believed to be linked to the poisoning spree which left 40 dogs dead….

JOHANNES PELSER - APCAN SECURITY

He was carrying a red bag with some implements in connection with housebreaking. We also found a bag with polony with some black grains that we presume is dog poison.

SOLOMON TEBE – APCAN SECURITY

After we searched him, the police arrived and we handed him over to the police.

VO – To protect their animals, dog owners are urged to keep them inside the house or in the backyard where they are less likely to be lured with poisoned food… that could very well be their last supper….


PROMOS

1> To silence barking dogs, criminals are using a banned pesticide sold openly on the streets. Security experts warn that dog poisonings are on the rise.

2> Stay alert… a poisoned dog in your home, could be a warning that criminals are scouting the area and your property could be their next target.

3> Why is one of the deadliest pesticides ever produced, capable of killing a grown man in a matter of minutes, being sold openly on the streets of Johannesburg?

Security experts warn that dog poisonings are on the rise. 2> Stay alert… a poisoned dog in your home, could be a warning that criminals are scouting the area and your property could be their next target. 3> Why is one of the deadliest pesticides ever produced, capable of killing a grown man in a matter of minutes, being sold openly on the streets of Johannesburg?

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We hold the SAPS accountable for failure to enforce laws regulate the use and possession of the highly toxic and prohibited substance Aldicarb.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Dr Verdoorn will illustrate the high toxicity of Aldicarb as well as the poison's effects not only on rats and dogs, but also on humans.
metadata.Summary: The Griffon Poison Information Centre (GPIC) says that dog deaths by poisoning are on the rise, and it is mainly due to a banned pesticide commonly used as rat poison. As many as 1 000 dogs die in SA each week due to poison. Aldicarb is a highly toxic pesticide that is illegal to use and possess in South Africa. However, people from neighbouring countries where the substance is still in use bring it into the country in bulk and sell it on the black market as rat poison. Aldicarb is notoriously known as 'two-step' (because you take 2 steps and you die) and 'aliphirimi' (the sun will not rise – because you will not see the next sunrise if you ingest it). It is deadly to rats, dogs and humans. Criminals often use Aldicarb to kill dogs at a property they wish to rob. The poison is placed inside sausages, wors or viennas, thrown over the fence for the dog to eat and criminals return some time later to rob the home, without the dogs alerting the sleeping owners. That is prevalent in the suburbs whereas in townships, many dogs die after accidentally ingesting Aldicarb which has been laid out in the open for rats. Aldicarb is easily available at most taxi ranks and some spaza shops and is preferred by many as rat poison because it is cheap. It sells for around R10 for a dosage which is enough to deal with rat infestation for the whole house, or kill an adult human.
metadata.Further information: We explore the high toxicity of Aldicarb and question why authorities are failing to eradicate the sale and use of the substance. This is an important discussion considering that the substance is also noted to be responsible for around 100 murders in Johannesburg each year and is also preferred as an effective poison to commit suicide. Our speakers expand on the dangers of Aldicarb not only to animals but also humans - Dr Verdoorn tells confirms the number above of 100 murders committed using Aldicarb in Johannesburg each year. Dr Verdoorn and Cora Bailey also give examples of when Aldicarb was used to commit suicide. The insert includes links that further highlight the seriousness of the consequences of using and being in possession of Aldicarb - it is literally a murder weapon for just R10 a pop, cheaper than murder weapons such as a gun and even a knife. We highlight this in our questioning to the police - if they would not ignore someone selling guns willy nilly on the streets, why are they then being so careless when it comes to Aldicarb salespeople, despite that the problem has around for many years. Another link will be done with the presenter interacting with dogs. All our speakers mention and one extensively discusses the criminality behind Aldicarb, dog poisonings and it being used as a murder weapon e.g. it being mixed in with the intended victim's popular food, the speed with which Aldicarb works (which makes it preferred for suicide). In our voice-overs we give examples of incidents of human deaths linked to Aldicarb. The SPCA also explains that when confronted with a high number of call-outs where dog poisoning is concerned, they alert the police as such incidents usually point to planned housebreakings. When filming the doctor's interview, he will show us just how little is needed to make the drug fatal to not just animals but more importantly to humans too. The insert also illustrates how easily available the drug is and that dealers are only too happy to sell the stuff in bulk. The SPCA and Cora share images of call-outs relevant to the topic and express their frustration at the prevalence of Aldicarb on the streets as well as police disregard for the Aldicarb use and possession. "Thabo" is a reformed housebreaker who cements the link between Aldicarb and crime by sharing how he used Aldicarb on many occasions when he went breaking into people's homes.
